title: 12 Tons Of KitKats Stolen From Truck Remain Unaccounted For - NewsBreak
text:
By Baila Eve Zisman ,
9 hours ago Last week in Europe, thieves stole over 400,000 KitKat chocolate bars from a truck.
The weight of the 413,793 stolen candy bars is equal to roughly 12 tons.
The truck was distributing the Nestle-manufactured chocolate bars along a route running from a factory in central Italy to Poland.
According to a statement from KitKat, “The vehicle and its contents remain unaccounted for, and investigations are ongoing in close collaborations with local authorities and supply chain partners.”
The company suspects that the missing candy bars may enter unofficial sales channels across European markets, and notes that each stolen candy bar is traceable through on-pack batch numbers. They have asked anyone who finds a match to alert the company.
KitKat’s spokesperson noted, “We’ve always encouraged people to have a break with KitKat – but it seem thieves have taken the message too literally and made a break with more than 12 tonnes of our chocolate.”
Subscribe To Our Cheat Sheet!One week of pop culture news in your inbox! “Whilst we appreciate the criminals’ exceptional taste, the fact remains that cargo theft is an escalating issue for businesses of all sizes.”
The statement continued, “With more sophisticated schemes being deployed on a regular basis, we have chosen to go public with our own experience in the hope that it raises awareness of an increasingly common criminal trend.”
On Sunday, KitKat posted the news to their Instagram account, adding, “The good news: there are no concerns for consumer safety, and supply is not affected.”
The comments on the Instagram post quickly flooded with references to the company’s tagline “Have a Break, Have a KitKat,” which has been used since 1957. Thousands of internet users made cheeky references to the jingle, writing quips like “It happened when the driver decided to take a break,” and “My bad guys I needed a break.”
KitKat in turn has capitalized on the event as a marketing opportunity, so much so that many Instagram users have commented their suspicions that the heist never even happened in the first place and was all simply promo for the brand.
Following the initial statement, KitKat posted a carousel slide of funny fan comments on the original post, captioning it, “DONT BREAK THE LAW ”.
The company followed up with two reels of an evidence board with yarn drawing connections between various headlines and sticky notes with quips like “Who needs a really big break?”
